riskReasons: The accepted name, Acer palmatum placement, green young bark and five-lobed green foliage are supported by institutional sources.
RHS separately accepts ‘Yamato-aoyagi’, resolving the principal near-name risk without treating it as a synonym.
Living-collection height exceeds the compact impression of some commercial descriptions, but this is a size-context issue rather than an identity conflict.

duplicateCheck.notes: Compared with RC-001–RC-010 and all other approved Catalogue assignments. ‘Aoyagi’ is distinct from the separately accepted ‘Yamato-aoyagi’, and from the red- or coral-stemmed RC-003 ‘Sango-kaku’ and CUL-000014 ‘Beni-kawa’. It is also not CUL-000024 ‘Arakawa’, whose mature rough bark is a different diagnostic. C0 resolves as unique.

identityNotes: The Atlas uses the accepted unhyphenated name ‘Aoyagi’. ‘Yamato-aoyagi’ is a separate RHS-accepted cultivar and must not be shortened or merged into this identity. Green bark and stems are descriptive comparison traits, not independent proof of cultivar identity.

content.summary: An upright, broad-topped Japanese maple notable for vivid pea-green young bark and stems, fresh green five-lobed foliage and deep yellow autumn colour, giving useful winter as well as leafy-season interest.
content.habit: Upright to spreading-branched deciduous tree with a broad crown. RHS describes a long-term tree to about 8 m, and a JC Raulston Arboretum plant was measured at 28 ft in 2022.
content.leafForm: Palmate leaves about 5 cm across, usually with five serrated lobes tapering to sharp points. The foliage is ordinary palmatum form rather than dissected or linearilobum.

seasonal.spring: Fresh green five-lobed leaves unfold with small purple-red flowers and developing red-flushed winged fruits.
seasonal.summer: Foliage remains fresh to medium green; young bark and stems provide the principal non-foliar diagnostic.
seasonal.autumn: Leaves turn deep yellow, while the green stem colour becomes especially conspicuous after leaf fall.

size.qualifier: RHS places the ultimate height within 4–8 m and spread within 2.5–4 m over 10–20 years. JC Raulston Arboretum recorded one long-established plant at 28 ft in 2022; this is a single-site measurement.

content.cultivation: Grow in moisture-retentive, well-drained soil in a sheltered position. Partial shade usually preserves foliage quality, though full sun can be tolerated where soil remains reliably moist. Avoid excessive exposure and drought that can cause leaf scorch.
content.diagnostic: ‘Aoyagi’ is compared by its pea-green young bark, ordinary five-lobed green leaves and yellow autumn colour. Do not confuse it with ‘Yamato-aoyagi’, with generic green-stem seedlings, or with coral-bark cultivars such as RC-003 ‘Sango-kaku’ and CUL-000014 ‘Beni-kawa’.
content.confidence: High confidence in accepted name, supported taxon, green-stem character, leaf form and yellow autumn colour. Moderate confidence in the generalised mature-size range because the living-collection measurement represents one site and age.
content.unresolvedIssue: The lean review did not establish original selection history or a primary diagnostic separating every green-bark cultivar. The intensity of green stem colour is expected to vary with age, season and exposure.
